questions.q: Why isn't 98.2% accuracy, by itself, a complete evaluation of this model?
options: Because accuracy can never be trusted for any model
Because it collapses every prediction into one number and can't show which specific predictions were wrong or whether the two kinds of mistake cost the same
Because 98.2% is actually a low score
Because accuracy only works for regression, not classification
questions.explain: Accuracy is a useful summary but hides which errors occurred — the confusion matrix and per-class metrics are needed to see whether the mistakes are the costly kind or not.

questions.q: In this capstone's confusion matrix ([[41, 1], [1, 71]]), what does the single "1" in the true-malignant row represent, and why does the lesson call it the costlier mistake?
options: A benign case incorrectly flagged as malignant, causing an unneeded follow-up test
A malignant case the model predicted as benign — a real cancer told it was nothing, which matters more in a screening context than a false alarm
A data entry error unrelated to the model
A sample that was dropped from the test set
questions.explain: The true-malignant row's off-diagonal cell is a false negative: a real malignant case predicted benign. In a medical screening context, missing a real cancer is more costly than a false alarm that just triggers extra testing.

questions.q: What does a recall of 0.976 for the malignant class actually mean here?
options: 97.6% of all 114 test predictions were correct
The model caught 41 of the 42 true malignant cases in the test set
97.6% of samples the model called malignant actually were malignant
The model's confidence score averaged 97.6%
questions.explain: Recall measures, out of all actual malignant cases, how many the model correctly identified — 41 of 42, or 97.6%. This is the same single miss the confusion matrix showed, expressed as a rate.

questions.q: What makes `LogisticRegression`'s coefficients useful for understanding this model, beyond just its accuracy?
options: They show exactly how much each feature pushes the prediction toward malignant or benign, letting you sanity-check that the model's reasoning matches real medical intuition
They reveal the exact original training images
They guarantee the model has no errors
They are purely decorative and have no interpretive value
questions.explain: The sign and magnitude of each coefficient show its pull on the prediction. Here, all top coefficients are negative and correspond to features (texture, area, radius, concavity) that pathologists associate with malignancy — a real, if informal, sanity check.

questions.q: Why does the lesson emphasize that classification_report's precision and recall numbers come from "the same 114 predictions" lesson 28 already made?
options: Because the model was retrained specifically to produce these metrics
To make clear these are different views of the same evaluation, not a new or separate test run — the metrics are computed from the exact predictions already generated
Because 114 is an unusually large test set
Because precision and recall require a different dataset than accuracy
questions.explain: accuracy_score, confusion_matrix, and classification_report are all just different summaries computed from the same y_test/y_pred pair — no new predictions are made to produce them.
